chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Nazarro's company and how he introduced the act
summary: Nazarro was an acrobatic understander with a little partner; Buck and Bubbles did their own act on his bill for over five years.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Initially, Buck and Bubbles were performing with the Nat Nazarro Brothers?

No, not Nazarro -- Nat Nazarro and his company. He had a boy, understand that worked with him. He had an understand that worked with him, there were no brothers. He hired a little fella that he could pick up and throw up and down to do a Hawaian trick or flag him up, he'd do tricks. I never seen anything like that. Well, that's what he had. They weren't brothers. He hired this little fella as an act to work with him on the stage. That's who he had working with him.
What were some of the routines that you did with him -- Nazarro?
our act. We did our act on the stage where he was. Do you see that, or do you?
Yeh. But initially the first time they would introduce you through their act and then you'd come on and do your thing.
I was just wondering if that lasted for long, or you started going solo without them --
No, no, that lasted long, that lasted over five years, that lasted.

Nazarro, not they -- Nazarro would introduce. He was the head man of the act. Nat Nazarro was the head man of the act. So he would be the one, the kid that worked with him didn't say nothing, didn't do nothing. He and the kid might talk something together but the kid ain't going to
say nothing the way we were concerned. The kid is just going to be along doing the act with him.
